title: Select a single field
task: Return only the value of the message field.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.message
explain: The single-value selector (.) returns the value of the first matching key.

title: Pick an item by index
task: Return the third environment in the array.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload[2]
explain: The index selector [n] counts from 0, so [2] is the third item.

title: Last item with a negative index
task: Return the last environment without hard-coding the array length.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload[-1]
explain: Negative indexes count from the end: -1 is the last item.

title: Range selector
task: Return the first two environments as an array.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload[0 to 1]
explain: The range selector [a to b] returns the items from index a to index b, both included.

title: Multi-value selector on repeated keys
task: The object has the key name twice. Return every name value as an array.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.*name
explain: payload.name would return only the first match ("Emilia"); .* returns all values for that key at this level, as an array.

title: Descendants selector
task: Collect every id, at whatever depth it appears.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload..id
explain: The descendants selector (..) finds a key at any depth. payload.id would return only 1.

title: Concatenate first and last name
task: Build a fullName field from firstName and lastName, separated by a space.
explain: ++ concatenates strings. This is the enrichment example from the first DataWeave session.

title: Upper and lower case
task: Return name in upper case and city in lower case.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  name: upper(payload.name),
  city: lower(payload.city)
}
explain: upper() and lower() change the case of a string.

title: Default for a missing number
task: Add number1 and number2. number2 is missing, so treat it as 0.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.number1 + (payload.number2 default 0)
explain: A missing key gives null. default supplies a fallback value, so the addition doesn't fail.

title: Script variable with var
task: Store the customer object in a script variable and build the id and the customer's full name from it.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
var c = payload.order.customer
---
{
  id: payload.order.id,
  name: c.first ++ " " ++ c.last
}
explain: A var declared in the header is used by its name (not vars.) anywhere in this script, and it shortens long paths.

title: if / else
task: Return the price and an action: "buy" if the price is below 100, otherwise "hold".
answer:
%dw 2.0
var action = if (payload.price < 100) "buy" else "hold"
output application/json
---
{
  price: payload.price,
  action: action
}
explain: if (condition) value else value is an expression. Here the result goes into a header variable, as in the tutorial.

title: Even numbers with filter
task: Keep only the even numbers.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload filter ((item, index) -> isEven(item))
explain: filter takes an array and returns an array of the items for which the lambda returns true.

title: Remove a key
task: Return the object without the password field.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload - "password"
explain: The - operator removes a key from an object. This interview question comes up often.

title: Split a string into an array
task: Split the string into words.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload splitBy " "
explain: splitBy turns a string into an array of strings, splitting on the given separator or regex.

title: Join an array into a string
task: Join the letters with hyphens under the key hyphenate.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ "hyphenate": payload joinBy "-" }
explain: joinBy is the opposite of splitBy: array to string, with a separator between the items.

title: == vs ~=
task: Compare number1 and number2 with both equality operators.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  strict: payload.number1 == payload.number2,
  similar: payload.number1 ~= payload.number2
}
explain: == needs the same type and value. ~= first coerces one value to the other's type, so 100 ~= "100" is true.

title: Default in string concatenation
task: Concatenate test1 and test2. test2 is missing, and the script must not fail.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.test1 ++ (payload.test2 default "")
explain: Without default you get "Unable to call ++ with (String, Null)". default "" replaces the null with an empty string.

title: Merge objects and arrays with ++
task: Merge the user and extra objects into one object, and join arrays a and b.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  merged: payload.user ++ payload.extra,
  all: payload.a ++ payload.b
}
explain: ++ works on strings, objects (merges the key-value pairs) and arrays (appends the items).

title: else if — buy, hold or sell
task: For each item return item and action: "buy" below 100, "sell" above 140, otherwise "hold".
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map ((p, i) -> {
  item: p.item,
  action: if (p.price < 100) "buy"
          else if (p.price > 140) "sell"
          else "hold"
})
explain: Chain else if for more than two outcomes. The final else handles every other case.

title: Pattern matching with match
task: Turn the action code into a message: buy, sell or hold, and "Invalid input" for anything else.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.action match {
  case "buy"  -> "Buy at market price"
  case "sell" -> "Sell at market price"
  case "hold" -> "Hold asset"
  else        -> "Invalid input"
}
explain: match works like switch: the first matching case wins, and else is the fallback.

title: Filter employees by salary ($ shorthand)
task: Return the employees who earn more than 50000.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload filter ($.salary > 50000)
explain: In filter, $ is the current item and $$ its index. The longer form is (item, index) -> item.salary > 50000.

title: filterObject on a key
task: Keep only the age key-value pair.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload filterObject ((value, key, index) -> key ~= "age")
explain: Object keys are of type Key, so key == "age" is false. Use ~= or (key as String) == "age".

title: map to value/index objects
task: Turn each letter into an object holding the letter and its index.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map { "value": $, "index": $$ }
explain: In map, $ is the item and $$ the index. This is the same as (i, ix) -> {value: i, index: ix}.

title: Rename keys for a DB insert
task: Rename the keys to the DB column names. emp_id must be a number, and emp_status is "active" or "inactive".
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map ((item, index) -> {
  emp_id: item.empId as Number,
  emp_name: item.empName,
  emp_status: if (item.empStatus == true) "active" else "inactive"
})
explain: map renames the keys of each record. as Number coerces the string, and if/else converts the boolean.

title: Upper-case all keys with mapObject
task: Convert every key to upper case and keep the values.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload mapObject ((value, key, index) -> { (upper(key)): value })
explain: mapObject transforms each key-value pair. A computed key must be in parentheses, or it is taken as the literal word.

title: Object to array with pluck
task: Turn each key-value pair into its own object, and also list the keys.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  pairs: payload pluck ((v, k, idx) -> { (k): v }),
  keys: payload pluck ((v, k) -> k)
}
explain: pluck takes an object and returns an array (object to array). reduce goes the other way.

title: Remove duplicates with distinctBy
task: Remove the duplicate record, using id.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload distinctBy $.id
explain: distinctBy keeps the first item for each distinct value of the criterion.

title: groupBy even/odd
task: Group the numbers by whether they are even.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload groupBy ((n, idx) -> isEven(n))
explain: groupBy returns an object of arrays, not an array. The keys are the group values, in order of first appearance.

title: Sort ascending and descending
task: Return the names sorted by age, youngest first and oldest first.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  asc: (payload orderBy $.age) map $.name,
  desc: (payload orderBy -$.age) map $.name
}
explain: orderBy sorts ascending. A minus in front of a numeric criterion sorts descending. Sort by a field, not by the whole object.

title: Sum with reduce — with and without an initial value
task: Sum the numbers with no initial accumulator, and again starting from 12.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  noInit: payload reduce ((i, a) -> a + i),
  withInit: payload reduce ((i, a = 12) -> a + i)
}
explain: With no initial value, the accumulator starts as the first item (5) and the loop begins at the second. With a = 12 it begins at the first item: 12+5+2+3.

title: flatten nested arrays
task: Remove the first level of inner arrays.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
flatten(payload)
explain: flatten merges the items of the first-level sub-arrays into the main array.

title: flatten only goes one level
task: Show the result of one flatten and of two.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  once: flatten(payload),
  twice: flatten(flatten(payload))
}
explain: flatten removes one level only, and it drops empty sub-arrays. Call it again for the next level.

title: Custom function
task: Write a named function add(n, m) and use it three times.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun add(n, m) = n + m
---
{
  a: add(1, 2),
  b: add(5, 2),
  c: add(100, 2)
}
explain: fun name(params) = expression, declared in the header, creates a reusable function.

title: Skip null fields
task: Map message and name. name is missing, so it must not appear in the output.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json skipNullOn="everywhere"
---
{
  message: payload.message,
  name: payload.name
}
explain: skipNullOn="everywhere" on the output line removes null values. It works for JSON and XML output, not CSV.

title: Change a date string's format
task: The date arrives as a dd-MM-yyyy string. Return it as yyyy-MM-dd, as dd-MMM-yyyy, and its year.
explain: First coerce the string to a Date using its current format, then format the Date as a String. MM is the month number, MMM the month name.

title: Number formatting
task: Format the amount with thousands separators and 2 decimals, show the price string with 2 decimals, and pad the code to 3 digits.
explain: Formatting a number means coercing it to a String with a pattern. A 0 always prints a digit, and a # only when needed.

title: Array of objects to one object
task: Convert the array into one object, with name as the key and id as the value.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload reduce ((item, acc = {}) -> acc ++ { (item.name): item.id })
explain: Array to object = reduce with an empty-object accumulator. Each iteration merges in one new key-value pair.

title: Count per group
task: Count the employees in each department.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload groupBy $.dept) mapObject ((v, k) -> { (k): sizeOf(v) })
explain: groupBy builds an object of arrays, and mapObject replaces each array with its size.

title: Merge two arrays by id
task: Add each employee's salary from the salaries array, matching on id.
explain: For each employee, filter the other array on the same id, take the first match with [0], and merge the field in with ++.

title: Rename keys with a mapping object
task: Rename fname to firstName and lname to lastName, and keep any other key as it is.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
var m = { fname: "firstName", lname: "lastName" }
---
payload mapObject ((v, k) -> { (m[k as String] default k): v })
explain: Look up each key in a mapping variable with a dynamic selector. If there is no entry the result is null, and default keeps the original key.

title: flatMap — map and flatten in one step
task: Using the docs cookbook function, map each item to an array (name 1 → none, name 2 → two new items, others → itself) and flatten the result.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun myExternalFunction(data): Array =
  if (data.name == 1) []
  else if (data.name == 2) [{name: 3}, {name: 5}]
  else [data]
---
payload flatMap ((item, index) -> myExternalFunction(item))
explain: flatMap = map followed by flatten, and the mapper must return an array. flatten(payload map ...) gives the same result.

title: Shift a timestamp to another time zone
task: createdAt is in UTC. Show it in India time as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ ist: ((payload.createdAt as DateTime) >> "Asia/Kolkata") as String {format: "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"} }
explain: >> moves a DateTime to another time zone (UTC+05:30 for India). CloudHub runs in UTC, so this is a common need.

title: XML to JSON with attributes
task: Return an array of books with their category attribute, title and year (as a number).
input:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<bookstore>
  <book category="cooking">
    <title lang="en">Everyday Italian</title>
    <author>Giada De Laurentiis</author>
    <year>2005</year>
    <price>30.00</price>
  </book>
  <book category="children">
    <title lang="en">Harry Potter</title>
    <author>J K. Rowling</author>
    <year>2005</year>
    <price>29.99</price>
  </book>
  <book category="web">
    <title lang="fr">Learning XML</title>
    <author>Erik T. Ray</author>
    <year>2003</year>
    <price>39.95</price>
  </book>
</bookstore>
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload.bookstore.*book map ((item, index) -> {
  category: item.@category,
  title: item.title,
  year: item.year as Number
})
explain: *book returns every book element as an array, and @category reads each item's attribute. XML values are strings, hence as Number.

title: JSON to XML with a single root
task: Write the books as XML under one bookstore root, one book element per item (compact, without the XML declaration).
explain: XML allows exactly one root, so wrap the output in a single-key object. An array value repeats its element for each item. indent=false and writeDeclaration=false only make the output compact.

title: JSON to XML with attributes
task: Write each book with its category as an attribute of the book tag (compact, without the XML declaration).
explain: element @(attr: value): content writes attributes. Mapping inside (...) spreads one book key per item into the root, so each book gets its own category.

title: CSV to JSON
task: Convert the CSV rows into JSON with employeeId as a number and name in upper case.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map ((item, index) -> {
  employeeId: item.empid as Number,
  name: upper(item.empname)
})
explain: Each CSV row becomes an object keyed by the header row. All CSV values are strings, hence as Number.

title: JSON to CSV with renamed columns
task: Write CSV with the columns renamed to employeeid and employeesalary.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/csv
---
payload map ((item, index) -> {
  employeeid: item.empid,
  employeesalary: item.empsalary
})
explain: output application/csv writes one row per object, with the keys as the header row.

title: read() a JSON string
task: The message arrived as plain text that holds JSON. Return its message field.
answer:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
read(payload, "application/json").message
explain: read parses a string or binary in the given format. Selectors work only after parsing. The S3 Get Object binary needs the same fix.

title: write() and read() round trip
task: Stringify the payload (as you would to store it in a DB text column), then read it back and return the type of the string and the name.
explain: write turns structured data into a String, where .name doesn't work. read turns it back into an Object.

title: Mask sensitive fields
task: Log the request payload with mobileNumber and memberId masked as #####.
answer:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::util::Values
output application/json
---
{
  "requestpayload": ((payload mask field("mobileNumber") with "#####") mask field("memberId") with "#####")
}
explain: mask comes from dw::util::Values and needs the import. Each mask's result feeds the next, and the field name must match the key exactly.
